problems.title: TrustyAI default-trustyai has field values from an earlier release
problems.description: The operator cannot apply TrustyAI default-trustyai: the stored object has field values of a type an earlier release used, and the installed CRD now expects another type. Kubernetes keeps a stored object as it was written, so the upgrade did not change it, and server-side apply cannot convert it. Until it matches, DataScienceCluster default-dsc stays not ready. Its module operator crash-loops because it cannot read the object either.
evidence: Field .spec.eval.lmeval.permitOnline: stored false; the installed CRD says string, one of allow, deny, default deny, optional
Field .spec.eval.lmeval.permitCodeExecution: stored false; the installed CRD says string, one of allow, deny, default deny, optional
CRD trustyais.components.platform.opendatahub.io's schema was last written by platform.opendatahub.io at 2026-11-01T10:00:00Z, the running operator

Module operator redhat-ods-applications/trustyai-operator-module-controller-manager is crash-looping (1061 restarts): its last exit says it cannot sync its informer for TrustyAI: last exit: Error (exit code 1): failed waiting for *v1alpha1.TrustyAI Informer to sync
problems.fix: Set each listed field to the installed CRD's default, or remove it where the CRD has none and it is optional (the table shows each change). The tool patches only these fields of TrustyAI default-trustyai, with your token, after a server-side dry run, and only if each still holds the value shown. The DataScienceCluster controller watches module CRs, so it applies the object again by itself.
problems.confirmMessage:
This patches TrustyAI default-trustyai:
- .spec.eval.lmeval.permitOnline: false -> "deny"
- .spec.eval.lmeval.permitCodeExecution: false -> "deny"

Each field is changed only if it still holds the value shown (a JSON Patch test), after the API server's dry run accepts the change. Nothing else changes.

problems.title: Deployment redhat-ods-applications/trustyai-service-operator-controller-manager must be recreated: its selector changed
problems.description: An earlier release created Deployment redhat-ods-applications/trustyai-service-operator-controller-manager with another spec.selector. Kubernetes does not allow changing a selector, so the operator cannot apply the current version and TrustyAI default-trustyai stays not ready. Deleting it lets the operator create it again with the current spec.
evidence: Operator error: unable to patch apps/v1, Kind=Deployment redhat-ods-applications/trustyai-service-operator-controller-manager: Deployment.apps "trustyai-service-operator-controller-manager" is invalid: spec.selector: Invalid value: {"matchLabels":{"app.kubernetes.io/name":"trustyai-service-operator","control-plane":"controller-manager"}}: field is immutable

Deployment redhat-ods-applications/trustyai-service-operator-controller-manager is owned by TrustyAI default-trustyai; the trustyai module operator redhat-ods-applications/trustyai-operator-module-controller-manager creates it again

Deployment redhat-ods-applications/trustyai-service-operator-controller-manager and its pods stop now; the trustyai module operator redhat-ods-applications/trustyai-operator-module-controller-manager creates it again with the current selector on its next reconcile, usually within seconds; the old ReplicaSets and pods are removed in the background.
problems.fix: Delete Deployment redhat-ods-applications/trustyai-service-operator-controller-manager so that the operator creates it again with the current selector. The tool deletes it with your token, only if it is unchanged since it was checked, and then waits up to 2m for it to come back ready.
problems.confirmMessage: This deletes Deployment redhat-ods-applications/trustyai-service-operator-controller-manager (propagation Background), after a server-side dry run, and only if its UID and resourceVersion are unchanged. Deployment redhat-ods-applications/trustyai-service-operator-controller-manager and its pods stop now; the trustyai module operator redhat-ods-applications/trustyai-operator-module-controller-manager creates it again with the current selector on its next reconcile, usually within seconds; the old ReplicaSets and pods are removed in the background.
problems.acknowledge: I accept that Deployment redhat-ods-applications/trustyai-service-operator-controller-manager is down until the operator creates it again: the tool cannot tell whether trustyai is in use: it has no reader for that component's resources.

problems.title: trustyai-operator-module-controller-manager is crash-looping (1061 restarts)
problems.description: Container manager keeps exiting and Kubernetes is backing off before restarting it.
evidence: Pod redhat-ods-applications/trustyai-operator-module-controller-manager-6d9f7c8b5-x2x7q, container manager, CrashLoopBackOff, 1061 restarts, age 9d: last exit: Error (exit code 1): failed waiting for *v1alpha1.TrustyAI Informer to sync
Likely caused by "TrustyAI default-trustyai has field values from an earlier release"
problems.fix: Read the logs of the previous run of the container (command below). A crash right after an update usually means the build is broken or a dependency is missing.
